aPropos.title: About us
aPropos.intro: Karriere Fähre is an international placement agency based in Douala, Cameroon, founded by a German-French-Cameroonian entrepreneur.
aPropos.missionBody: Building a reliable bridge between talent from Central Africa and German companies facing a skilled-labor shortage, through training, integration preparation, and support at every step of placement.
aPropos.founderTitle: A founder who knows both sides
aPropos.founderBody: Having grown up between Germany and Cameroon, our founder understands both the demands of the German labor market and the aspirations of Cameroonian talent. Karriere Fähre (literally "the career ferry") carries that bridge in its name.
aPropos.value2: High standards in training and candidate preparation
aPropos.distingueLead: An agency built for both shores, with a genuine command of the German framework.
aPropos.dist1Body: Rooted in Central Africa and connected to the real needs of German companies.
aPropos.dist2Body: Skilled Immigration Act, Chancenkarte, qualification recognition (Anerkennung).
aPropos.dist3Body: From A1 up to the required level, supporting even candidates starting from scratch.
aPropos.dist4Body: Recruitment that respects people and origin countries alike, for the long term.
aPropos.ethiqueTitle: Ethical recruitment, on both sides of the bridge
aPropos.ethiqueHeading: We follow the WHO Code of Practice
aPropos.ethiqueBody1: International recruitment of professionals, especially in healthcare, must be responsible. We rely on the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel: we don't recruit at the expense of countries whose essential systems are fragile.
aPropos.ethiqueBody2: In practice, that means transparent pathways, informed candidate consent, and a win-win relationship between Central Africa and Germany.
aPropos.ethiqueNote: Reference: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel.
aPropos.equipeLead: A German-Cameroonian team that knows both realities: that of African talent and that of German employers.
aPropos.equipeNote: This section will be completed with real photos and team bios before launch.

aPropos.doorsTitle: Which side of the bridge are you on?
aPropos.doorsText: Whether you want to work or train in Germany, or you're looking to recruit, we support you.
aPropos.doorsCandidat: I want to work / train in Germany

aProposFaq.a1: Karriere Fähre is a German-Cameroonian placement agency based in Douala. We connect qualified talent and aspiring trainees from Central Africa with German companies facing labor shortages, with German training and full support.
aProposFaq.q2: What does the name "Karriere Fähre" mean?
aProposFaq.a2: "Karriere" means "career" and "Fähre" means "ferry" in German. Together: "the career ferry", the image of a boat connecting two shores, just as we connect Central Africa and Germany.
aProposFaq.a3: Our agency is based in Douala, Cameroon, with a primary focus on Central Africa and a direct connection to the needs of German companies.
aProposFaq.a4: Yes. We rely on the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, so as not to weaken essential systems in origin countries and to ensure transparent, consented pathways.
aProposFaq.q5: Do you support candidates who don't speak German yet?
aProposFaq.a5: Yes. We offer built-in language training, from A1 up to the level required by the trade, supporting even candidates starting from scratch.

aProposHistoire.title: Our story
aProposHistoire.subtitle: How Karriere Fähre grew out of a journey between two countries.
aProposHistoire.section1Body: Our founder grew up between Germany and Cameroon. She saw, on one side, German companies struggling to hire for essential jobs, and on the other, Cameroonian talent ready to train and contribute, but without a reliable bridge to connect them.
aProposHistoire.section2Body: Karriere Fähre was founded in Douala to close that gap: an organization that knows German requirements (language, qualification recognition, legal framework) and Cameroonian realities (training, support, trust) from the inside.
aProposHistoire.section3Body: "Fähre" means "ferry" in German. Like a ferry connects two shores, Karriere Fähre connects two labor markets, one candidate and one company at a time.

aProposMethode.title: Our method
aProposMethode.subtitle: A structured process, from first contact through to integration in Germany.
aProposMethode.section1Body: Every candidate takes a German placement test before any placement promise is made. We guide them to the right path, Fast Track or Full Training, rather than making unrealistic claims.
aProposMethode.section2Body: Our German courses follow the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), with preparation for exams recognized by employers and German authorities.
aProposMethode.section3Body: On the company side, every account is validated by our team before any access to the candidate pool. On the candidate side, every profile is reviewed before becoming visible to partner companies.
aProposMethode.section4Body: Our role doesn't stop at the signed contract: we stay available during visa procedures and the first steps in Germany.

candidats.title: Working or training in Germany, supported at every step
candidats.subtitle: In short: there are three legal paths to working in Germany from Cameroon: skilled employment, vocational training (Ausbildung), and the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte). Karriere Fähre assesses your profile, trains you in German, and prepares every step up to departure.
candidats.kick: Candidate area · Cameroon & Central Africa → Germany
candidats.voiesTitle: What are the paths to working in Germany?
candidats.voiesLead: Three legal paths lead to Germany, depending on your qualification, experience, and German level. Here's how they differ, and which one fits you.
candidats.voie1Body: You already have a recognized qualification or professional experience.
candidats.voie2Body: You're young and want to learn a trade on the job, directly within a company.
candidats.voie3Body: You want to come look for a job on the ground, with no contract at departure.
candidats.voie3Tag2: Up to 1 year on-site to search
candidats.tableRow5Val3: Up to 12 months to find work
candidats.tableNote: The exact thresholds (points, language level per occupation) evolve with German regulations. We check them for your case during the assessment.
candidats.eligibiliteTitle: Am I eligible to work in Germany?
candidats.eligibiliteLead: You're likely eligible if you're between 18 and about 40, have a qualification or professional experience, and are willing to learn German up to the required level. Four things matter:
candidats.crit1Body: A qualification (even a Cameroonian one) or solid experience in a sought-after trade. We help get it recognized.
candidats.crit2Body: B2 is our standard, for skilled employment and for the Ausbildung alike. Don't have it yet? Our courses take you there from scratch.
candidats.crit3Body: Most paths target 18-40 year-olds, with Ausbildung geared more toward younger candidates. Each case is reviewed individually.
candidats.crit4Body: Success depends as much on preparation as on drive. We support those who commit seriously.
candidats.accompagnementLead: From your first assessment to your integration in Germany, we handle every step. Seven services, one single point of contact: you never have to navigate the process alone.

candidats.metiersTitle: Which occupations are hiring most in Germany?
candidats.metiersLead: Germany lacks skilled workers in healthcare, construction and trades, hospitality, industrial and technical trades, and IT. These are the sectors where your profile holds the most value.
candidats.statText: Germany faces a lasting shortage of skilled workers across many sectors, which drove the reform of its immigration law and the introduction of the Chancenkarte.
candidats.formationsTitle: Two training paths, depending on your level
candidats.formationsLead: Starting from scratch in German, or already at the level and want to be ready for the German job market? We have a path for every situation.

candidatsComment.title: How it works
candidatsComment.subtitle: Four clear steps between your sign-up and your departure for Germany.
candidatsComment.section1Body: You create your candidate profile and take a German placement test, oral and written.
candidatsComment.section2Body: Already B2: you join our candidate pool directly. Below B2: you follow our full A1 → B2 training program.
candidatsComment.section3Body: Once your profile is validated by our team, it becomes visible to our German partner companies looking for your skills.
candidatsComment.section4Body: Visa procedures, departure preparation, first steps in Germany: we stay by your side at every stage.

candidatsEligibilite.title: Am I eligible?
candidatsEligibilite.subtitle: The basic criteria for joining the Karriere Fähre program.
candidatsEligibilite.section1Body: Be of legal age and have a serious plan to train or settle professionally in Germany.
candidatsEligibilite.section2Body: No level is required at sign-up. If you're already at B2, you go straight to placement. Otherwise, you follow our A1 → B2 training path.
candidatsEligibilite.section3Body: We prioritize shortage occupations in Germany: healthcare, hospitality, construction, industry and technical trades, IT. A qualification or experience in one of these fields is an advantage.
candidatsEligibilite.section4Title: Not sure? Let's talk it through
candidatsEligibilite.section4Body: The best way to know where you stand is a direct conversation. Book an appointment, no obligation.

candidatsDiplomes.title: Qualification recognition
candidatsDiplomes.subtitle: What to know before getting your qualification recognized in Germany.
candidatsDiplomes.section1Body: For many regulated occupations (healthcare in particular), Germany requires your diploma to be recognized as equivalent to a German one before you can practice.
candidatsDiplomes.section2Body: We help you identify the right authority for your occupation and target region, gather the right documents, and anticipate any upskilling measures required.
candidatsDiplomes.section3Title: What this means for your timeline
candidatsDiplomes.section3Body: Recognition can take several months. We factor it into your path from the start to avoid surprises on the visa and employer side.

candidatsVivre.title: Living in Germany
candidatsVivre.subtitle: What to expect once you're there, beyond the job.
candidatsVivre.section1Body: Registering with local authorities (Anmeldung), opening a bank account, finding housing: we prepare you for these steps before departure.
candidatsVivre.section2Body: B2 level lets you work, but daily life keeps demanding effort. We encourage continued learning once you're there.
candidatsVivre.section3Body: Karriere Fähre stays reachable after your arrival to guide you through any question or integration difficulty.

candidatsFaq.title: Candidate FAQ
candidatsFaq.subtitle: The most frequently asked questions about our program.
candidatsFaq.q1: Is Karriere Fähre paid for candidates?
candidatsFaq.a1: Terms vary by path (Fast Track or Full Training). Contact us or book an appointment to discuss the details.
candidatsFaq.q2: Do I need to already speak German to sign up?
candidatsFaq.a2: No. You can sign up with no prior knowledge and follow our full A1 → B2 path.
candidatsFaq.q3: How long does the full path take?
candidatsFaq.a3: About 10 months of training (A1 to B2), plus 1 month of exam preparation.
candidatsFaq.q4: Does Karriere Fähre guarantee a job in Germany?
candidatsFaq.a4: We guarantee serious support and matching with real partner companies. Final placement also depends on your profile and the interview with the employer.
candidatsFaq.a5: We prioritize shortage occupations in Germany (healthcare, hospitality, construction, industry, IT). Your profile and preferences are taken into account during matching.
candidatsFaq.q6: What happens if I don't reach B2 level?
candidatsFaq.a6: We adjust the training pace. Placement only happens once the required level is reached.

coursAllemand.title: German course: Full Training (A1 → B2) or Fast Track
coursAllemand.subtitle: Karriere Fähre trains candidates in German up to the level German employers require. Two tracks structured around the Common European Framework (CEFR): Full Training takes those starting from zero or an intermediate level from A1 to B2; Fast Track is for profiles already certified at B2 and focuses on professional fine-tuning before placement.
coursAllemand.pourquoiTitle: Your German level decides which route is open to you
coursAllemand.pourquoiLead: German isn't a formality: it's the criterion that opens or closes each route to Germany. Here's what each one requires.
coursAllemand.voie1Body: B2 required, along with a recognised qualification or relevant experience.
coursAllemand.voie2Body: B2 required to start a dual apprenticeship.
coursAllemand.voie3Body: A1 minimum: the higher your level, the more points you score.
coursAllemand.voiesNote: Exact thresholds shift with German regulations and the target occupation. We check them for your case during the assessment.
coursAllemand.forkTitle: Two tracks to Germany, depending on your German level
coursAllemand.forkLead: Depending on whether you're starting from zero or already have the required level, we offer you one of these two tracks.
coursAllemand.quizTitle: Full Training or Fast Track: which track is right for you?
coursAllemand.quizSubtitle: Answer in 30 seconds to find the training track that fits your level.
coursAllemand.quizQ2Title: Do you have a German certificate (Goethe / telc)?
coursAllemand.quizQ2o1: Yes, a B2 less than 12 months old
coursAllemand.quizQ2o2: Yes, a B2 more than 12 months old
coursAllemand.quizQ3o2: I already speak it, I want to work fast
coursAllemand.quizResFullText: You build your German from A1 to B2, at an intensive pace, up to the level employers expect. The full course, designed for starting from zero or consolidating an intermediate level.
coursAllemand.quizResFastText: You already have the level: we confirm your B2, sharpen your professional German, then take you straight to placement.
coursAllemand.fullPageTitle: Full Training: the complete German course, A1 to B2
coursAllemand.fullPageSub: The intensive track to start from zero or consolidate an intermediate level, up to the B2 German employers require — with sub-levels, pace and exams in detail.
coursAllemand.fastPageTitle: Fast Track: already B2, straight to a job in Germany
coursAllemand.fastPageSub: For profiles already certified at B2: professional fine-tuning, interview preparation, then direct placement with our partner companies.
coursAllemand.quizPageTitle: Which German track is right for you? The quick test
coursAllemand.quizPageSub: Full Training or Fast Track? Three questions, 30 seconds, and you know which track fits your level.
coursAllemand.fullCardBody: You're starting out or at an intermediate level. We take you to B2 over about 10 months, before your placement.
coursAllemand.fastCardBody: You're already at the required level. You skip the course and join our pool directly for placement.
coursAllemand.fastTitle: Already at B2? Here's your track
coursAllemand.fastLead: If you already have a certified B2, you don't need the full course. We confirm your level, sharpen your professional German, then take you through to the job.
coursAllemand.fastIncl2: Sharpening the technical vocabulary of your trade
coursAllemand.fastIncl3: Simulations of professional situations in German
coursAllemand.fastStep1Body: A placement test, spoken and written, checks that you're genuinely at the B2 employers expect.
coursAllemand.fastStep2Body: Your profile joins our pool of candidates ready to be presented to German partner companies.
coursAllemand.fastStep3Body: We present you to the employers whose role fits your profile, and arrange the interviews.
coursAllemand.fastStep4Body: As for all our candidates, we handle the recognition of your qualification, the visa file and departure preparation.
coursAllemand.fastNote: Your B2 isn't certified yet? We can prepare you for the exam to strengthen your file.
coursAllemand.parcoursLead: Each CEFR level is broken into sub-levels and taken as a group, at an intensive pace. You move up one stage at a time to B2, the level employers expect — in about ten months, without stretching your plan over years.
coursAllemand.rythmeText: 4 hours of class a day, 5 days a week — 20 hours a week, in a small group of 5 to 7 people max.
coursAllemand.a1Body: Understand and use familiar everyday expressions, introduce yourself, ask simple questions about your immediate surroundings.
coursAllemand.a2Body: Understand isolated sentences on close-to-home topics (family, shopping, work), exchange simple information about routine tasks.
coursAllemand.b1Body: Cope on your own in most everyday situations, produce simple connected speech, describe an event and explain a plan.
coursAllemand.b2Body: Understand the main ideas of concrete and abstract topics, interact with a native speaker fluently and spontaneously. This is the level expected to work.
coursAllemand.prepBody: A dedicated month after B2, focused on the format of your chosen exam: comprehension, written and spoken production, time management.
coursAllemand.totalNote: That's roughly 10 months of teaching, plus 1 month of exam preparation.
coursAllemand.metierTitle: German aimed at your occupation, not just at grammar
coursAllemand.metierBody1: Beyond general language, our courses cover the professional vocabulary of your sector and real everyday situations in Germany.
coursAllemand.metierBody2: Student file, badge, tracked attendance: we prepare our candidates with the same rigour expected in a German workplace.
coursAllemand.examensTitle: A certificate recognised by employers and authorities
coursAllemand.examensLead: Goethe-Institut, TELC, ÖSD, TestDaF for B2. A B1 exam is available on request. We point you to whichever fits your target occupation and region.
coursAllemand.finalText: We assess your real level, spoken and written, then place you in the right group — starting at A1 if you're beginning from zero.

ausbildung.title: Ausbildung in Germany: the springboard to a paid trade — and university
ausbildung.subtitle: The Ausbildung isn't an end, it's a springboard. Germany's dual vocational training: paid from the first month, a recognised qualification at the end, no qualification needed to start. And after two to three years of experience, university opens up — trade first, studies next.
ausbildung.exploreTitle: The Ausbildung journey, section by section
ausbildung.card1Body: The trades by sector, with length, requirements and pay.
ausbildung.card2Body: What you need: age, German level, a training place.
ausbildung.card3Body: The springboard to skilled work — and, with experience, university.
ausbildung.condPageTitle: The entry requirements for an Ausbildung in Germany
ausbildung.condPageSub: Age, German level, diploma, training place: what you need for an Ausbildung — and what Karriere Fähre takes on.
ausbildung.apresPageTitle: After the Ausbildung: from skilled worker to university
ausbildung.apresPageSub: The Ausbildung isn't an endpoint — it's a springboard. In Germany a learned trade opens the door to university, without the Abitur: around 70,000 people studied this way in 2023. Technician to engineer, carer toward healthcare and even medicine: the degree follows the experience.
ausbildung.ctaConditions: The entry requirements for an Ausbildung
ausbildung.quoiTitle: An Ausbildung is not an internship
ausbildung.quoiLead: It's the German vocational training system, and the most common way in for a young person who hasn't trained in a trade yet.
ausbildung.quoi1Title: You're an employee, not a student
ausbildung.quoi1Body: You sign a training contract with a German company and are paid every month, from the first year.
ausbildung.quoi2Body: You learn the trade on the job at the company, and the theory at the vocational school (Berufsschule).
ausbildung.quoi3Title: A recognised qualification at the end
ausbildung.quoi3Body: After three years you hold a qualification recognised across Germany — and you become a Fachkraft.
ausbildung.conditionsTitle: What you need to line up for an Ausbildung
ausbildung.conditionsLead: Less demanding on qualifications than people assume, more demanding on language and age.
ausbildung.cond1Body: That's the whole point of this route: you don't need a recognised qualification to start. A secondary school leaving certificate is enough.
ausbildung.cond2Body: The age limit for the Ausbildung visa was raised to 35 in March 2024 (§ 16a of the German Residence Act).
ausbildung.cond3Body: B2 is our standard: it's what lets you follow the vocational school and understand your trainer from day one. Our courses take you there, even from scratch.
ausbildung.cond4Body: You need a contract with a German company before you leave. That is exactly what we go and find for you.
ausbildung.conditionsNote: Exact thresholds shift with German regulations, the trade, and the chamber responsible. We check them for your case during the assessment.
ausbildung.langueBody1: Without the language there is no visa, no training place, and no vocational school you could follow. It's the first step, and it's the one we walk with you from zero.
ausbildung.langueBody2: Our course takes you from A1 to B2 in roughly 10 months, plus one month of exam preparation.
ausbildung.etapesTitle: From your application to your first day
ausbildung.etape1Body: Age, schooling, motivation: we check that the Ausbildung really is your route.
ausbildung.etape2Body: From A1 to B2, with the vocabulary of the trade you're aiming for.
ausbildung.etape3Body: We put your profile in front of German companies hiring apprentices.
ausbildung.etape4Body: Training contract signed, then the Ausbildung visa file and the embassy appointment.
ausbildung.etape5Body: Settling in, first days at the company and the school, and our follow-up on the ground.
ausbildung.apresTitle: The Ausbildung isn't an end — it's a springboard
ausbildung.apresQuote: You were taught to choose: studies OR a trade. In Germany it's a trade THEN studies — both.
ausbildung.apresIntro: It's not a slogan. Germany recognises a \u201cthird path\u201d to university, open to the vocationally qualified — governed since 2009 by the standing conference of education ministers (KMK).
ausbildung.univBody: In Germany two routes lead to university without the Abitur. You enter the country first — a trade, a salary, integration; higher study can follow.
ausbildung.payeLine: Get paid (often €1,000 to €1,400/month), learn the language, gain experience… then study.
ausbildung.path1Body: A Meister or Techniker — an advancement qualification — grants the same university access as the Abitur and opens engineering studies.
ausbildung.path2Body: With an advancement qualification (Fachwirt), the exam grade replaces the Abitur when you apply — including for human medicine and dentistry.
ausbildung.route1Body: Meister, Techniker or Fachwirt: these upgrades open university across all fields, with the same access as the Abitur.
ausbildung.route2Body: A learned trade and around three years of experience open university in your field, often after an aptitude test. In some states (Berlin, Bremen, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate), the completed Ausbildung alone is now enough.
ausbildung.apresStat1Label: students without the Abitur in Germany (2023)

ausbildung.apresSource: Sources: Standing Conference of Education Ministers (KMK, 2009 resolution); Federal Statistical Office and CHE — studieren-ohne-abitur.de, 2023 data.
ausbildung.finalText: The trade, the salary, then university: send your application — we support you at every step.

visa.title: Visa for Germany: the right route depending on your path
visa.subtitle: In short: there isn't one Germany visa but several, each tied to a route — skilled employment, Ausbildung or the Chancenkarte. Karriere Fähre identifies yours and assembles the whole file, right up to the embassy appointment.
visa.introTitle: The visa follows from your route, not the other way round
visa.introLead: You don't pick a visa at random: it depends on your profile and the route that fits you. Identify your route, and the right visa follows.
visa.typesLead: Three situations, three visas. Here's which one fits which profile.
visa.type1Body: You have a recognised qualification and a job offer in Germany, with no age limit. This is the skilled employment (Fachkräfte) route.
visa.type2Body: You want to train in a trade through an apprenticeship, with no prior qualification and under 35. The Ausbildung visa opens this route.
visa.type3Body: You have a recognised qualification but no job offer yet. The opportunity card lets you come and look for work on the spot, on a points system.
visa.roleTitle: The visa file is our job — not yours
visa.roleLead: The visa is the stage where many plans fail when you're on your own. We take it on from end to end.
visa.role1Body: We prepare the Anerkennung, the trickiest step, from the start of the journey.
visa.role2Body: Supporting documents, forms, translations: we build a complete, compliant file.
visa.role3Body: Booking the embassy appointment and preparing you for the interview.
visa.role4Body: When the employer allows it, § 81a (the beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren) gets recognition and visa handled as a priority.
visa.delaisTitle: Realistic timelines, stated from the start
visa.delaisBody: Timelines depend on the route, the country and how loaded the authorities are. We don't promise miracles: we give you a realistic schedule from the first assessment, and activate the accelerated procedure where it's available.
visa.finalText: Recognised qualification, job offer, German: the skilled-worker visa rewards a profile that's ready. See the conditions in detail and have yours assessed.

visaChancenkarte.title: Chancenkarte: come to look for qualified work in Germany
visaChancenkarte.subtitle: In short: the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) lets you come to Germany for up to a year to look for qualified work, with no offer to start. Admission runs on a points system — six points minimum.
visaChancenkarte.quoiTitle: A visa to look for work on the spot
visaChancenkarte.quoiLead: Introduced in June 2024, the Chancenkarte is for qualified people who don't yet have an employer in Germany.
visaChancenkarte.quoi1Title: Up to a year on the spot
visaChancenkarte.quoi1Body: You come to look for qualified work directly in Germany, with the right to work part-time (up to 20 hours a week) to support yourself.
visaChancenkarte.quoi2Body: Unlike the skilled worker visa, you don't need a signed contract before you leave.
visaChancenkarte.quoi3Body: Admission depends on a points system that rewards your qualification, experience, language level and age.
visaChancenkarte.baseTitle: What you need before the points even apply
visaChancenkarte.baseLead: Three conditions must be met first. Only then does the points system come into play.
visaChancenkarte.base1Body: A university degree recognised in your country, or vocational training of at least two years.
visaChancenkarte.base2Body: German A1 minimum, or English B2. At Karriere Fähre we take you beyond that, up to B2 in German.
visaChancenkarte.base3Body: You must prove you can fund yourself during the search, for example through part-time work (up to 20 hours a week).
visaChancenkarte.pointsTitle: How to reach the six points
visaChancenkarte.pointsLead: Six points minimum are required. Each criterion earns points, with one caveat: some don't stack — for language, for instance, the highest level is the one that counts.
visaChancenkarte.p1Label: Partial recognition of your qualification, or permission to practise a regulated profession
visaChancenkarte.p2Label: Five years of qualified experience (within the last seven years)
visaChancenkarte.p4Label: Two years of qualified experience (within the last five years)
visaChancenkarte.p8Label: A prior stay of at least six months in Germany
visaChancenkarte.pointsNote: Source: official criteria under § 20a AufenthG (the Chancenkarte points system), in force since June 2024. The system may change; we check your actual score during the assessment.
visaChancenkarte.roleTitle: We work out your points and build the file
visaChancenkarte.roleBody: The points system looks simple on paper, but each criterion has its conditions. We assess your real situation, spot the points you're missing — often the language — and build the file with you.
visaChancenkarte.disclaimer: These criteria are German law (§ 20a AufenthG), provided for information and subject to change. Only the German authorities decide on granting the Chancenkarte; we help you put forward the strongest possible file.
visaChancenkarte.finalTitle: Is the Chancenkarte right for you?
visaChancenkarte.finalText: Gather the points, prepare your file and apply: we support you from the Chancenkarte all the way to the job.

visaTravailleur.title: Skilled worker visa for Germany: requirements and procedure
visaTravailleur.subtitle: In short: with a recognised qualification and a job offer in Germany, the skilled worker visa (Fachkräftevisum) opens the doors — with no age limit. Recognition, file, accelerated procedure: we take it all on.
visaTravailleur.quoiLead: The skilled employment (Fachkräfte) route, governed by §§ 18a-18b of the German Residence Act.
visaTravailleur.quoi1Body: A degree or vocational training recognised as equivalent in Germany (Anerkennung).
visaTravailleur.quoi2Body: A contract or firm offer from a German employer, in your field.
visaTravailleur.quoi3Body: Unlike the Ausbildung, this visa sets no maximum age.
visaTravailleur.condLead: Three things shape your file — we support you on each.
visaTravailleur.cond1Body: Your foreign qualification must be recognised as equivalent. The trickiest step, which we prepare from the start.
visaTravailleur.cond2Body: A role matching your qualification, at a market-rate salary.
visaTravailleur.cond3Body: A level sufficient for the role, often B2. Our courses take you there from zero.
visaTravailleur.accelBody: Your employer can launch the beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren with the central immigration authority: recognition and visa are then handled as a priority, cutting timelines significantly.
visaTravailleur.accelNote: New in 2024: the Anerkennungspartnerschaft even lets you come and work first, then complete the qualification recognition on the ground.
visaTravailleur.roleTitle: The file is our job — not yours
visaTravailleur.finalText: The Chancenkarte lets you come and look for a qualified role on the spot, with no contract to start.

travailler.title: Working in Germany: 163 occupations can't fill their jobs
travailler.subtitle: Germany isn't pretending to recruit. Its Federal Employment Agency puts it plainly: 163 occupations are short of skilled workers, and around 440,000 qualified positions sit open. Health, construction, technical trades, transport — the need is real, and so is the pay. Between you and these jobs stand the language, the recognition of your qualification and the visa. That's exactly what we prepare with you.
travailler.condLead: Working in Germany as a qualified professional comes down to four conditions. None is out of reach — that's exactly what we prepare you for, step by step.
travailler.cond1Body: A diploma or vocational training whose equivalence is confirmed in Germany: this is the Anerkennung. It's the centrepiece of your file and the most technical step — we prepare it with you from the start.
travailler.cond2Body: B2 is the standard level employers and authorities expect — it opens the most doors. Even from scratch, we take you from A1 to B2, with the vocabulary of your trade.
travailler.cond3Title: A job offer — or the Chancenkarte
travailler.cond3Body: The skilled-worker visa requires a contract matching your qualification. No offer yet? The Chancenkarte, a points-based system, lets you come and look for a job on the spot.
travailler.cond4Body: Once recognition and offer are in place, the visa (§ 18a-18b) is issued — often via the fast-track procedure run by your future employer. The last step before departure.
travailler.contexteTitle: Germany can't do it alone anymore
travailler.contexteLead: The country is ageing and its economy is running at full tilt. The result: it's short of workers. Don't take our word for it — the Bundesagentur für Arbeit, Germany's Federal Employment Agency, counts shortages in 163 of around 1,200 occupations. Nearly one in eight.
travailler.contexteBody: In 2024, around 440,000 qualified positions were registered, nearly half of them in these shortage occupations: health and care, construction and trades, truck driving, early-childhood education. These jobs go unfilled locally. Your profile belongs precisely here.
travailler.contexteNote: Source: Bundesagentur für Arbeit, shortage-occupation analysis (Fachkräfteengpassanalyse) 2024.
travailler.exploreTitle: What working in Germany actually means
travailler.card1Body: Health, technical, engineering, IT, transport: the sectors under the most strain, with the German job titles and the level expected.
travailler.card2Body: Housing, first steps, daily life: what awaits you once you arrive, and our support that continues.
travailler.cadreTitle: A legal framework that protects you
travailler.cadreBody1: By reforming its Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz), Germany opened its doors wide — even creating a state portal, \u201cMake it in Germany,\u201d to welcome you. Working there by the book means the same rights as a German employee: market-rate pay, social security, paid leave, job security.
travailler.cadreBody2: No grey area, no empty promises. A proper contract, a proper visa, rights guaranteed by law — that's the only way we place our candidates.
travailler.finalText: Send us your profile. Together we review your qualification, your level of German and your target occupation, then map out your path: recognition, language, visa.

partirCameroun.title: Moving to Germany from Cameroon
partirCameroun.subtitle: In short: from Cameroon, the path to Germany runs through German, the recognition of your qualification and the visa lodged in Yaoundé via VFS Global. Karriere Fähre, based in Douala, supports you at every step — on the ground.
partirCameroun.avantageBody1: Karriere Fähre is established in Douala (Bonamoussadi). You don't have to prepare your departure alone from home: the German training, your profile assessment and the file preparation happen here, in person.
partirCameroun.avantageBody2: That's the difference from a remote agency: a contact close to you, who knows both the Cameroonian reality and the German requirements.
partirCameroun.parcoursTitle: From Douala to Germany, step by step
partirCameroun.etape1Body: It all starts with the language. We take you to the required level, our standard being B2, even from scratch.
partirCameroun.etape2Body: We prepare the Anerkennung of your qualification, the trickiest step, ahead of the visa.
partirCameroun.etape3Body: We build your file and support you for lodging it in Yaoundé, via the VFS Global centre.
partirCameroun.etape4Body: Departure preparation, first steps in Germany and follow-up once you're there.
partirCameroun.visaTitle: Where and how to lodge your application
partirCameroun.visaBody1: For Cameroon, the national visa application is lodged in Yaoundé with the German mission, through the provider VFS Global. Since late 2025, a reinforced VFS Global centre in Yaoundé has increased processing capacity (students, trainees and skilled workers).
partirCameroun.visaBody2: The procedure runs through the online Videx form, then an appointment to submit your file and fingerprints. VFS Global receives the file; the decision to grant the visa or not rests solely with the German embassy, which may call you for an interview.
partirCameroun.visaNote: Sources: German Embassy Yaoundé and VFS Global (2025-2026). The terms, fees and timelines change: we check the current state for your file and never replace the embassy's decision.

formationsAllemand.section1Body: A1, A2, B1, then B2: each level follows the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), with groups progressing together over about 2 to 3 months per stage.

formationsExamens.section1Body: A recognized certificate (usually B2 level) is generally required for the work visa and directly reassures the employer about your actual level.
formationsExamens.section2Title: One dedicated month, at the end of the path
formationsExamens.section2Body: After reaching B2, one month of intensive preparation (about 80 hours) prepares you specifically for the format of your chosen exam.
formationsExamens.section3Body: We guide you toward the exam best suited to your target occupation and destination region. A B1-level exam is available on request.

formationsIntegration.section2Body: If you already have some German but targeted gaps, we offer a shorter upskilling track instead of repeating the full A1 → B2 path.
formationsIntegration.section3Body: This preparation continues after your arrival in Germany, alongside our post-departure support.

metiers.title: The occupations hiring in Germany
metiers.subtitle: Germany is short of qualified professionals across whole sectors — health, construction, hospitality, industry, IT, logistics. Already have a trade? These sectors are waiting for you. We get your qualification recognised, bring you to the required level of German, and open the door to a skilled position.

metiers.contexteBody: If you already hold a qualification, that means open positions across several sectors and a clear path to reach them: diploma recognition, language, skilled-worker visa. That's our job.

metiers.eligibiliteLead: Whatever the sector, four things shape your plan, and we help with each one:

metiers.crit2Body: A qualification, a diploma, or solid experience in the trade.
metiers.crit3Body: We prepare the Anerkennung of your qualification, the trickiest step.
metiers.crit4Body: Employers look for profiles that settle for the long term.
metiers.parcoursTitle: From application to job, in 4 steps

metiers.finalTitle: Find the occupation that fits you
metiers.finalText: Get your profile assessed: we'll tell you which sector and path suit you, and what steps lie ahead.

metiersFaq.q1: Which occupations are hiring most in Germany?
metiersFaq.a1: Healthcare, construction and trades, hospitality, technical industry, IT, and logistics are among the sectors under the most pressure.
metiersFaq.a2: B2 level is required for all our paths. We support you up to B2, even starting from scratch.
metiersFaq.a3: Depending on the path: a recognized qualification, a professional certification, or solid experience can open doors. We assess your profile to find the right path.
metiersFaq.a4: Many occupations require recognition (Anerkennung). We build the file with you to avoid mistakes that cost months.
metiersFaq.q5: How do I know which sector fits me?
metiersFaq.a5: Get your profile assessed: based on your qualification, experience, and German level, we guide you to the sector or sectors best suited to you.
